stories.title: Election Commission holds crucial meeting amid SIR row, announces key decisions

article_sentences: NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Saturday said all decisions taken on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, including the nationwide exercise, were approved unanimously, while announcing measures to simplify the process for voters facing notices over discrepancies.

The clarification comes amid row over report that claimed differences within the EC over SIR of electoral rolls." In the recent months, the Commission has taken numerous decisions including SIR across the country.
The order for the SIR issued on 24.6.2025 for all the States/UTs, starting with Bihar, followed by West Bengal and 30 other States/UTs was issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission.
The same has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India vide its order dated 27.5.2026.
The schedule for SIR for 12 States and UTs was issued on 27.10.2025 and those for 19 States/UTs was issued on 14.05.2026 with the unanimous approval of the Commission.
The final figure of number of electors will be known only after final publication in the remaining 12 states of Phase-III," the poll body said in a statement.

At a meeting held on Saturday, the Commission decided that voters who receive notices during the ongoing SIR over being unmapped or having logical discrepancies will not ordinarily have to appear before the electoral registration officer (ERO).
Booth-level officers (BLOs) will visit their homes to collect documents and upload them on ECINet for the ERO to decide.
Hearings will be held only in exceptional cases, preferably online.
An adult family member can also attend a hearing on behalf of the elector if authorised.
The Commission said facilities for online hearings would be strengthened.

The Commission also directed district election officers to set up help desks and special camps for people living in night shelters, labourers, poor people and homeless persons, depending on local requirements.

- He argued that the Commission could not change the form unilaterally and said two.
Election Commissioners had sought its withdrawal.
- The Congress leader urged the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognisance and hold Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar accountable.

Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh on Saturday questioned a change to the online voter registration process, alleging that the Election Commission had added a mandatory declaration to Form 6 without following the procedure required to amend it.

In a post on X, Ramesh said the online form was altered in early July to ask applicants whether their parents or grandparents had been included in an earlier Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
He called the change “totally illegal” and said it could make registration harder for young and first-time voters.
Ramesh contrasted the new requirement with the Election Commission’s direction to officials to organise special enrolment camps for young voters and publicise them on social media.
He argued that encouraging registration while adding a further condition to the online process was contradictory.
Citing the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, Ramesh said the power to amend Form 6 lay with the central government, not the Election Commission acting on its own.
He claimed that any change to the prescribed form would require an amendment to the rules and communication to Parliament.
The rules, including Form 6, are published by the government.

stories.title: Supreme Court orders sealing of over 16,000 properties, demolition of illegal structures in Meerut
stories.summary: A Bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K.V. Viswanathan also formed a judicial commission, led by former Supreme Court judge Justice Sudhanshu Dhulia, to conduct a thorough inquiry in Uldepur, on the outskirts of Meerut, regarding the nature of land where these illegal residential colonies have developed
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: Taking serious note of illegal constructions and the conversion of residential properties for commercial use, the Supreme Court has directed the Uttar Pradesh government to seal over 16,000 properties in Meerut and demolish unauthorised structures.

A Bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K.V. Viswanathan also formed a judicial commission, led by former Supreme Court judge Justice Sudhanshu Dhulia, to conduct a thorough inquiry in Uldepur, on the outskirts of Meerut, regarding the nature of land where these illegal residential colonies have developed.

"We are shocked and disturbed to learn, reading the status report, that hundreds of illegal residential colonies have come up at Uldepur," the Bench said, after perusing the report by P. Guruprasad, Chairman of Uttar Pradesh Awas Evam Vikas Parishad.
The Bench noted that the department has undertaken an inspection and survey of various parts of Meerut.
The report showed that the town has been divided into four zones: Zone-A, Zone-B, Zone-C, and Zone-D.
"In Zone-A, 16 teams deputed for the purpose of inspection/survey have identified 16,726 structures to be absolutely illegal/unauthorised.
Out of 16,726 structures, 12,907 comprise residential, 874 residential-cum-non- residential, and 2945 non-residential constructions," it noted in its September 21 order.

The top court, hearing a contempt petition related to non-compliance with previous directives on illegal constructions, instructed the authorities to take appropriate action against all the 16,726 illegal structures in Zone-A at the earliest.
"The first step in the process is to ask the occupants to vacate the premises and to seal all these premises, i.e., the 16,726 illegal structures.
We direct accordingly.
It is possible that some of these structures may be in a dilapidated condition and may collapse, resulting in casualties.
We do not want this to happen at any cost.

stories.headline: Maharashtra declares 265 of 358 talukas drought-hit, announces relief
stories.title: Maharashtra declares 265 of 358 talukas drought-hit, announces relief
stories.summary: The Maharashtra government on Saturday declared 265 of the 358 talukas in the state as drought-affected, announcing relief measures, including restructuring of crop loans, concession in land revenue and deferment of recovery of agriculture-related loans. According to a government resolution issued late on Friday, this covers 74 per cent of the state. The decision follows Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis's recent visit to some drought-affected parts of the state. The state government has activated 'Trigger-1' under its manual for drought management 2016 (updated in 2020) and Drought Management Code to declare drought conditions and initiate relief. Trigger-1 is the first stage in the state's drought framework, activated by a rainfall deficit of more than 25 per cent combined with a prolonged dry spell of 21 days. stories.headline: Substance abuse among children is a child protection issue: CJI Surya Kant
stories.title: Substance abuse among children is a child protection issue: CJI Surya Kant
stories.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Saturday said substance abuse among children must be understood as a child protection issue, rather than as a matter of public health concern. Delivering the Pataliputra Pragya Pravah lecture on 'Childhood Beyond Drugs: Protection, Care and Reintegration' at the Bihar Lok Bhavan here, Justice Kant cited a recent Lancet study to say that at least one in five teenagers in India were at moderate to high risk of substance abuse. "Substance abuse among children must be understood not only as a matter of public health concern, but as a child protection issue as well," he said. Justice Kant stressed the need for a "child-sensitive response" to addiction to protect not only the child's physical and mental well-being but also their dignity and sense of self-worth. He said, "Restoration means creating conditions in which a child can again experience what childhood ought to provide -- education, relationship, play, trust, and the confidence of a future bey

stories.headline: Supreme Court Dismisses BJP MLAs' Plea Challenging Quashing Of Corruption Complaint Against Karnataka Energy Minister KJ George
stories.title: Supreme Court Dismisses BJP MLAs' Plea Challenging Quashing Of Corruption Complaint Against Karnataka Energy Minister KJ George
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (25 September) dismissed a Special Leave Petition (SLP) against the Karnataka High Court's judgment which had quashed criminal complaint against Karnataka's Energy Minister KJ George and Bangalore Electricity Supply Company Limited (BESCOM) officials over alleged irregularities in the tender procurement and installation of smart electricity meters in Karnataka.

A bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran declined to interfere with the High Court's order, holding that there existed “no good ground to interfere with the impugned order passed by the High Court.”

A criminal complaint was filed against Minister KJ George and BESCOM officials, by three MLAs (CN Ashwath Narayan, SR Vishwanath, and Dheeraj Muniraj) of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), alleging offences under Sections 314, 316, and 61 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), and Section 13(1)(a), 13(1)(b) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (PC Act), in connection with the tender for smart meters.
The MLAs had first approached the Lokayukta police before filing the complaint before the PC Act Special Court.

On George's petition seeking quashing of the proceedings, the Karnataka High Court had quashed the proceedings reasoning that it had found no material to substantiate the corruption allegation, and no allegation of any pecuniary benefit having been received by the Minister.
Aggrieved by the High Court's ruling, the BJP MLAs filed an SLP before the Supreme Court.
“Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and having gone through the materials on record, we find no good ground to interfere with the impugned order passed by the High Court.”
For Petitioners: Mr. Lakshmy Iyenger, Sr. Adv.; Mr. Dhawesh Pahuja, AOR; Mr. Saket Gogia, Adv.; Mr. Aakash Vt, Adv.; Mr. Harshith S, Adv.; Ms. Gauri Pande, Adv.; Mr. Mansingh, Adv.
Mr. Deepesh Meena, Adv.; Mr. Adithya KS, Adv.; Ms. Harshita Singh Tomar, Adv.
For Respondents: Mr. Kapil Sibal, Sr. Adv.; Mr. Vivek Jain, AOR; Ms. Suchitra Kumbhat, Adv.
Mr. Rohit H Nair, Adv.; Ms. Ishika Gandhi, Adv.; Mr. Shathabish Shivanna, Adv.; Mr. Abhishek Janardhan, Adv.; Mr. Samrudh Suraj Hegde, Adv.
